analyzed_vuln.description: In the FMT_STRING (%s/%p) path, `len` is initialized from `RSTRING_LEN(str)` and later potentially modified using precision (`len = p - RSTRING_PTR(str)` with `prec` as signed mrb_int). There is no validation that the resulting `len` is non-negative before `PUSH(RSTRING_PTR(str), len)` at line ~617, which eventually reaches memcpy with a signed value converted to size_t. With crafted format input, this produces a negative length (seen as -1773790777) and triggers ASan negative-size-param in memcpy.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The mruby_fuzzer loads attacker-controlled bytes directly as Ruby source (`mrb_load_string`). The PoC `%\x10%.11111111111s\x10%9` drives execution into Kernel.sprintf/format (`mrb_f_sprintf` -> `mrb_str_format`) with malformed format specifier/arguments so that the string-formatting branch computes an invalid negative `len` and then calls `PUSH(..., len)`, causing memcpy with negative size. No special harness state is required beyond providing this input script.
